book_title: Al-Muhannadī: A Guide to Lawful Living

preface.title: How This Book Came to India — and Why It Still Speaks

chapters.title: The Dignity of Earning Your Bread
chapters.rationale: Opens with the scriptural and prophetic praise of work, trade, and providing for one's dependents, before the book turns to the table.

chapters.title: At the Table: Eating, Feeding, and Being Fed
chapters.rationale: A single social arc from the manners of eating, through the merit of feeding others, to the reciprocal etiquette of guest and host.

chapters.title: Clean and Unclean: Meat, the Knife, and the Hunt
chapters.rationale: The seam turns from courtesy to substance — what may be eaten, how an animal is slaughtered, what the hunt yields, and what may be worn.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of a Sale
chapters.rationale: The book's first sustained commercial section: the three pillars of a valid sale, the conditions of the object sold, and disputes over price.

chapters.title: Lending Without Riba
chapters.rationale: Loans split by intention into worldly and otherworldly, the Qur'anic ban on riba, dealings with non-Muslims, orphans' property, and bankruptcy.

chapters.title: Trusts, Pledges, and Shared Walls
chapters.rationale: The remaining property contracts — rental, partnership, pre-emption, loan for use, deposit, mortgage, and the division of shared buildings and land.

chapters.title: Why Marry at All
chapters.rationale: The argument against celibacy and monasticism, the household as the first school, and the conditional license of plural marriage.

chapters.title: Choosing Well, Looking Rightly
chapters.rationale: From the real home built by husband and wife to the choice of a partner, the age of marriage, community endogamy, the veil, proposal, and the permitted glance.

chapters.title: The Contract: Forbidden Degrees, Guardians, and the Bride-Price
chapters.rationale: The legal machinery of marriage — who may not be married, who may contract it, what may be stipulated, the mahr, and the mutual rights of spouses.

chapters.title: Milk, Maintenance, and the Untying of a Marriage
chapters.rationale: Nursing-kinship and its prohibitions lead into support of the household, the missing husband, and the forms of dissolution — divorce, khul', and the waiting period.

chapters.title: What Outlives You: Charity, Endowment, and Inheritance
chapters.rationale: The closing movement gathers spending in God's way, gifts and perpetual waqf, the making of wills, and the prescribed shares of the estate.
